bugs: routes/api.php:6 puts the API routes in the `web` middleware group, so the session, cookies and CSRF all apply to /api/posts. I swapped in a PreventRequestForgery that doesn't skip under unit tests, and an authenticated POST /api/posts returned 419. Any JSON client without an XSRF token gets 419 on every write, and the test suite can't see this because CSRF is skipped when running unit tests.
PostController.php:40,53: authorization runs inside the action, after the FormRequest has already validated. A non-author who sends an invalid payload gets 422 instead of the 403 the spec asks for.
StorePostRequest.php:18: `tags.*` has no `required`, so null or blank entries produce confusing double errors ('must be a string' plus 'has a duplicate value' on the nulls).
Guest request to /api/posts without an Accept: application/json header returns 500, because route('login') is undefined. All three implementations share this.
antipatterns: routes/api.php:6 mixes the `web` middleware group into API routes.
app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:22-32 trims tags by hand in prepareForValidation. The global TrimStrings middleware already does this, including nested arrays.
app/Http/Requests/UpdatePostRequest.php:5,12 extends StorePostRequest only to pull one rule out with `parent::rules()['status']`, and still repeats the tags rules. This inheritance is awkward.
app/Http/Requests/UpdatePostRequest.php:10-11 uses `sometimes|string` without `required`, so title and body depend on ConvertEmptyStringsToNull to reject empty strings.

strengths: Thin controller using apiResource, Gate::authorize and a JsonResource. Store returns 201 implicitly through wasRecentlyCreated.

Observer handles unique slug generation with a fallback for empty slugs, and sets published_at only if it is missing.
Index uses `latest()->latest('id')` as a tiebreaker, `whereRelation` for the tag filter, `withQueryString`, and validates per_page.
Tests exercise PATCH, freezeSecond and the published_at preservation path.

strengths: Authorization uses route `->can('update', 'post')` middleware, so it runs before FormRequest validation and non-authors get 403 even with invalid payloads (tested at PostApiTest.php:204).

v.rationale:
All three share most of their design: enum status, #[Fillable]/#[ObservedBy]/#[Scope] attributes, an observer for the unique slug and published_at, a policy, FormRequests, JsonResource with tag names, and `latest()->latest('id')` pagination. All suites pass (impl-1: 20 tests, impl-2: 26, impl-3: 30). The ranking came down to what the probes found.

impl-3 ranks first. It authorizes with route `->can()` middleware, so non-authors get 403 before validation runs. That is the exact requirement, and it has a test. It also has the most complete tests. Its faults are minor: hand-written routes with no PATCH (405), a redundant setStatusCode(201), and a hand-rolled enum accessor.

impl-2 is the most idiomatic in its details: `$request->enum`, apiResource, slug route key, `distinct` validation and a composite index. But it calls Gate::authorize inside the action, after the FormRequest has validated. A non-author sending an invalid payload gets 422 instead of 403, which I confirmed with a probe. It also duplicates a postAttributes helper.

impl-1 shares impl-2's authorization-ordering issue and adds a more serious one. It puts API routes in the `web` group, and with CSRF enforced as in production, an authenticated JSON POST returned 419. It also has awkward FormRequest inheritance (`parent::rules()['status']`), trims tags by hand even though TrimStrings already does, confusing errors for null tags, and the thinnest test suite.

All three return 500 for a non-JSON guest request because no login route exists, so that issue doesn't affect the ranking.
